strengths: Novel generation-plus-verification RAG paradigm that addresses real limitations of embedding-based retrieval methods in capturing semantic dependencies
Efficient suffix array-based verification with O(log N) complexity enabling practical deployment and processing 500K samples in 2 hours instead of 2.5 days
Large-scale dataset contribution of 500,000+ samples with formal library dependencies, promised to be open-sourced
Comprehensive experimental evaluation with multiple baselines, ablation studies, multi-attempt stability analysis, and difficulty-stratified results
Consistent empirical improvements in both retrieval metrics (85% precision for DDR vs 3-12% for R@5) and downstream BEq scores across test sets
Clear presentation with effective visualizations (Figure 1) and well-motivated problem formulation
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: suffix arrays and SFT are standard techniques; the contribution is primarily engineering-focused combination rather than algorithmic innovation

Unfair baseline comparisons: DDR uses Qwen3-32B while RA baseline uses 7B model, confounding retrieval method with model capacity. Only one embedding-based method (topological-informativeness) compared; no dense retrieval or other recent methods
Implausibly poor baseline performance (R@5 precision 0.03-0.12, recall 0.09-0.19) raises concerns about baseline tuning. No explanation for why these methods perform so poorly

Evaluation methodology issues: (1) Suffix-based matching criterion conflates full/partial names (Nat.sqrt and Int.sqrt both match 'sqrt'), potentially inflating DDR precision; (2) Dataset extraction process not validated for quality; (3) Possible data leakage using extracted dependencies from FineLeanCorpus for training and testing
Incomplete ablation studies: Missing analysis of (a) fine-tuning contribution vs. base model + verification, (b) training data size scaling, (c) LLM generation quality without suffix array filtering
Unsubstantiated generalization claims: Methodology evaluated only on Lean 4 + Mathlib; no experiments with other theorem provers (Coq, Isabelle) despite claiming transferability

Acknowledged incompatibility: DDR cannot retrieve metadata (documentation, usage examples), making it incompatible with Liu et al. (2025b)'s framework. Workaround (setting fields to None) is inelegant

Small test sets (200 samples per split) without significance testing or confidence intervals. Modest improvements on hardest problems (BEq 0.31→0.38 on Diff89) limit practical impact where help most needed
Missing error analysis: No investigation of (a) types of missed dependencies, (b) false hallucinations that pass verification, (c) failure modes of the generation component
Difficulty ordering integrity questioned: Diff0 and Diff1 show anomalously high difficulty contradicting the scale definition, yet this issue is not thoroughly investigated

Suboptimal experimental choices: Temperature 0.7 for deterministic autoformalization task; Diff45 shows unexplained performance peak despite higher difficulty; incomplete connection between retrieval metrics and downstream task improvements

strengths: Well-motivated problem: Clearly identifies concrete limitations of existing autoformalization approaches (poor contextual awareness, low retrieval precision/recall, inability to scale)
Novel generation-plus-verification paradigm: DDR leverages LLM capabilities directly to generate dependencies rather than selecting from embeddings, avoiding expensive encoder training
Elegant algorithmic design: Suffix array verification achieves O(log N) complexity, enabling practical deployment and efficient dataset construction (2.5 days → 2 hours)
Valuable dataset contribution: 500,000+ sample dataset with formal library dependencies; extraction methodology is generalizable to other corpora

Comprehensive experimental evaluation: Multiple baseline classes, multiple metrics (precision, recall, F1, TypeC, BEq), ablation studies with statistical reporting (standard deviations), evaluation across difficulty levels
Substantial empirical improvements on retrieval task: DDR precision 0.85-0.93 vs R@5 baseline 0.02-0.12 (Table 2); demonstrates clear advantages in multi-attempt reliability and generation efficiency
Clear presentation: Well-written with effective visualizations; methodology is detailed and reproducible
Honest acknowledgment of limitations: Forthrightly discusses inability to retrieve supplementary metadata in Section 5
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: Suffix arrays are well-established algorithmic primitives; core contribution is applying existing techniques to autoformalization rather than developing fundamentally new methods

Significant unresolved limitation: DDR cannot retrieve supplementary metadata (documentation, code usage, type signatures) that existing methods provide; workaround of setting fields to None represents meaningful information loss; incompatibility with Liu et al. (2025b) framework limits practical adoption

Modest downstream performance gains: While retrieval improvements are substantial, autoformalization gains are incremental (e.g., Table 3 Diff89: 0.38 BEq vs 0.31 for baseline = 22% relative improvement); connection between retrieval quality and formalization quality insufficiently analyzed

Limited scope and unvalidated generalization claims: Evaluation exclusively on Lean 4/Mathlib; despite claims methodology is 'generalizable,' no empirical validation on other theorem provers (Coq, Isabelle, Mizar) or domains

Experimental design confounds: DDR base model (Qwen3-32B) has 4.5× more parameters than RA baseline (InternLM2-Math-Base-7B); fair comparison requires matched model sizes; moreover, using FineLeanCorpus for both training data extraction and evaluation creates data contamination concerns despite difficulty-based splitting

Insufficient error analysis: No breakdown of failure modes, investigation of which dependency types DDR struggles with, analysis of false positives (dependencies passing suffix check but semantically incorrect), or false negatives (missed dependencies)

Suffix matching evaluation criterion concerns: Pragmatic but potentially imperfect; no empirical analysis of whether suffix matching produces semantically incorrect alignments (e.g., 'sqrt' matching Nat.sqrt, Real.sqrt, Int.sqrt); no independent verification that BEq alignment with human judgment holds in this context

Missing implementation details: Exact suffix array construction algorithm not specified; computational cost comparison (inference latency, memory) not thoroughly discussed; generation prompts provided but full decoding details incomplete

Theoretical justification underdeveloped: Limited formal analysis of why LLMs should generate better dependencies than selecting from embeddings; connection to LLM contextual understanding capabilities could be more rigorous

Reproducibility limitations: Qwen3-32B model access may be restricted; dataset marked 'to be open-sourced' but not available for review; some baselines require implementations from external papers; baseline methods (R@5, R@10) may not be optimally tuned for this setting

strengths: Well-motivated problem addressing real hallucination and low retrieval precision issues in autoformalization
Novel generation-plus-verification paradigm that is conceptually cleaner and more scalable than embedding-based selection
Efficient Suffix Array Check (SAC) verification mechanism with strong complexity improvements (O(sM log N) vs O((s+d)MN))
Comprehensive experimental validation across multiple models, difficulty levels, and both SFT/ICL settings demonstrating consistent improvements
First systematic quantification of hallucination in LLM outputs for dependency retrieval, showing ~30% hallucination in baselines vs ~1-5% in DDR
Strong empirical results: precision 0.8-0.9 vs 0.2-0.5 for competitors, with plug-and-play applicability across different autoformalizers
Useful 500k+ sample dataset with generalizable construction methodology for the community
Good reproducibility with detailed hyperparameters, prompts, and experimental setup provided
weaknesses: Limited core technical novelty: SAC is from prior work (Liu et al. 2024), and DDR is standard SFT on Qwen3-32B; the main contribution is applying SAC in a new loop, which is incremental engineering rather than conceptual innovation

Significant data leakage concerns: DDR trained and tested on same corpus (FineLeanCorpus) with only difficulty-based splits; no analysis of train/test distribution overlap, raising questions about generalization

Questionable evaluation metrics: the suffix-based matching criterion (substring + component sublist) is loose and could artificially inflate precision numbers (0.8-0.9 seems surprisingly high); this criterion lacks independent validation
Output format incompatibility: DDR generates abbreviated names while downstream RA model requires full metadata, limiting practical utility and explaining modest downstream improvements in some cases
Insufficient explanation of why DDR works: no investigation into which problem characteristics drive retrievability, limited failure case analysis, and missing ablations on design choices

Moderate downstream improvements: some cases show minimal gains (Claude-3.5-Sonnet Diff01: 0.070→0.070), and comparisons with R@5/R@10 are somewhat unfair since they output different formats and are inherently non-hallucinatory by design

Crude semantic verification: SAC only checks existence, not semantic appropriateness; dependencies could exist but be contextually irrelevant, and binary verification provides no ranking or confidence
No statistical significance testing or confidence intervals; temperature=0.7 suggests variance in the top-8 sampling but this isn't analyzed
Limited generalization: only evaluated on Lean 4 + Mathlib; claims about other formal corpora and theorem provers are speculative without experimental validation
Missing dataset URL and incomplete open-source contribution declaration
